functions.scope:
Paired isolated fixtures only; symmetric collaborators do not certify collaborator internals or full-game behavior. Fixture domain and collaborator boundaries from README: # InteriorBase

Estado: validaciÃ³n final de fixtures aprobada por el coordinador; informe `20261008-092631-221476`, 25600 pares. El alcance se limita a los fixtures y colaboradores documentados.

Checks list search, all tile states 0..12, invalid/edge coordinates, positive/zero/negative rectangles, forced/protected changes, window conversion, early whole-function return on status3, corner branches and strip scan directions. GetTileStatus compares the complete EAX int32 return, including upper bytes; CheckTilesEmpty retains its declared int8 contract. Full 0x794-byte object snapshots use lossless hexadecimal strings; result and hook side must match exactly. Object pointer fields are normalized to identical markers only after checking exact receiver binding to the original box buffer and expected list head; both sides must preserve those bindings. Funciones: Exit (592230), AddGotoPt (591D20), AddInteriorInfo (591E40), GetBoundingBox (593DB0), CalcExitPts (5924A0), Furnish (591590). Evidencia: `../InteriorEvidence/Interior_<nombre>.txt`, pseudocodigo REA y ensamblador completo del EXE canonico.

Compara todos los bytes del interior, incluida la direccion m_box: ambos lados utilizan exactamente la misma direccion del fixture. No normaliza ni elimina punteros. Conserva los bytes del box, los cuatro puntos de salida y las trazas ordenadas. GetTileStatus y SetTilesStatus permanecen reales porque el EXE inserta parte de sus operaciones; GetTileCentre, FindBoundingBox, transformacion de direccion, eliminacion de pickups y despachadores de decoracion usan callbacks EXE/DLL simetricos.

Fixtures con coordenadas .1/.3, capacidad16, tiles0..7, direcciones-1..5 y decoracion0..7 ejercitan entradas positivas y negativas. CalcExitPts mantiene pares de goto ordenados y puertas presentes/ausentes. Los colaboradores aislados y los grafos sinteticos limitan la cobertura: no acredita generacion completa de muebles, busquedas arbitrarias ni memoria invalida.

El cierre restaura cada hook y su bloqueo, destruye los parches RAII y compara los cinco bytes originales de cada entrada. `state_restored` solo es verdadero si esas comprobaciones pasan; cualquier fallo produce evento terminal error. Root controla compilacion y GTA serial. No se ha relajado el analizador.

Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. functions.scope: Simple pair bench inside the full game (original with the hook off vs candidate with the hook on), 2304 isolated CPU pairs for 4 functions, zero differences, natural completion event with state_restored, saves unchanged, configs restored, per-function coverage thresholds met. CAEAudioHardware::Initialise runs on a FAKE 0x1100-byte CAEAudioHardware (pseudo-random fill per case, identical in both passes); the real AEAudioHardware is never touched. DirectSoundCreate (EXE IAT 0x85801C target) and DirectSoundCreate8 (DLL import) are patched in dsound.dll only during the call and return a fake COM device (QueryInterface/AddRef/Release, GetCaps, SetCooperativeLevel and GetSpeakerConfig with scripted HRESULTs and capabilities); the real device is never opened. operator new (EXE 0x82119A, to which the DLL one forwards) is patched only during the call and hands out blocks of a 1 MiB arena pre-filled with 0xCD (other threads are forwarded to the original), so the REAL constructors of the loaders and channels run (EXE vs DLL) and are compared block by block (offset, size, FNV hash; the vtable pointer, dword 0, of the channel blocks of size 0x90 and 0x60098 is masked). Compared for CAEAudioHardware::Initialise: return value (AL), hash of the whole fake object, arena blocks, arena bytes used, the fade-thread buffer count (0xB610E8), the user-track scan state (0xB6B988) and the trace of every stubbed call with normalised arguments. Traced stubs, patched at the EXE address and at the DLL body, so these helpers get NO credit: CAEAudioHardware::InitDirectSoundListener, CAEMP3BankLoader::Initialise, CAEMP3TrackLoader::Initialise, CAEStreamingChannel::Initialise, CAEAudioChannel::SetVolume, CAEUserRadioTrackManager::ScanUserTracks and Initialise, CAESmoothFadeThread::Initialise and Start, CAEStreamThread::Initialise and Start, CAEAudioHardware::LoadSoundBank and LoadSound, CAEAudioUtility::GetRandomNumberInRange<int>, CAESoundManager::AreSoundsOfThisEventPlayingForThisEntity and CancelSoundsOfThisEventPlayingForThisEntity; IsForegroundApp parks the real streaming thread during the bench. No audio thread is created or started. Declared limits: (1) after a stubbed MP3 bank or track loader Initialise returns false the DLL writes an NOTSA_LOG_ERR message (spdlog allocates through operator new) that the EXE does not have; from that point the trace, the block list and the arena usage are frozen (Freeze()), so allocations or stubbed calls made by the DLL after that failure are not detected through those channels, only through the object hash, the return value and the compared globals; (2) the path with m_nUserTracksScanState == IN_PROGRESS (Sleep(100) loop) is not tested, scan states used are OFF, COMPLETE, ERROR, 4, -1 and INT_MAX; (3) DirectSoundCreate is replaced by a fake COM device, so the real DirectSound behaviour is not exercised; (4) the constructors of channels and loaders run for real (EXE vs DLL) but are not validated here and are only compared as a side effect. Source corrected to what the EXE does before this run: CAEAudioHardware::Initialise uses operator new(0x6E4) plus Constructor() for CAEMP3BankLoader (the EXE only writes 0x14 and 0x66A, 0x4DFB10); CAEFrontendAudioEntity::Initialise writes the fields that were missing (0x80, 0x82=0x1C, 0x7E=-1, 0x84..0x94) and LoadSound takes a signed byte id (movsx). An earlier run (20261009-005347-353159, probe 17c9d956...) failed with 341 differences in 1536 CAEAudioHardware::Initialise pairs, all of them only in arena_used, blocks and recs (the NOTSA log allocations of limit 1); it is kept rejected as hashes only. Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Function-specific: Corpus 1536: DirectSoundCreate HRESULT E_FAIL (1/8), S_FALSE (about 1/7) or S_OK; SetCooperativeLevel HRESULT 0x88780078 (1/8), S_FALSE or S_OK; GetCaps E_FAIL (1/4) or S_OK with random DSCAPS; random speaker config; dwFreeHw3DAllBuffers cycling {0,1,0x17,0x18,0x19,0x1F,0x30,0x3F,0x40,0x41,0x1000,0xFFFFFFFF} around the 0x18/0x40 thresholds; listener, bank loader and track loader initialise success 7/8 each; auto-scan byte 0, 0x80 or 1; scan state {0,2,3,4,-1,INT_MAX}; random initial fade count. Coverage in the approved run: 777 cases reach CAEStreamThread::Start (759 stop earlier), 573 with hardware mixing (>= 0x18) and 204 without, ScanUserTracks reached in 529.

C3dMarkers::LoadUser3dMarkers) and DoScriptSetupAfterPoolsHaveLoaded (0x5D3390); CPools::Load is scripted false/true. These helpers get NO credit; only the own logic of each function is validated. The 'file' is a std::vector and the 'FILE*' an opaque token; the work buffer is allocated by the open double with the game operator new[] and freed by the function under test (otherwise by the bench after noting work_null). The returned value, ordered trace of outgoing calls with raw arguments, x87 control word and all fixture bytes are compared. Excluded/limits: ReportError blocks 25, 26 and >= 28 (the EXE uses an uninitialised buffer); ms_WorkBufferSize kept at 0xC800 in GenericLoad (with a smaller value the EXE reads past the 5-byte header), its effect covered only in LoadDataFromWorkBuffer-org; work-buffer sizes below 0xC800 are sanitised to pos = kBuf to avoid the EXE's own infinite recursion; the NOTSA branch of GenericLoad (save-version check) is not exercised because the Extract double returns the current version, and the NOTSA block 25/26 names in ReportError are left as deviations. In ReportError the EXE formats with sprintf (0x821BB5, replaced) into a local buffer while the DLL emits the same text through spdlog (captured with a temporary logger sink). Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Function-specific: Corpus 208: 26 blocks x 8 codes (0,1,2,3,4,255,-1,INT_MAX); no message for codes > 2; blocks 25, 26 and >= 28 excluded.

functions.source_provenance: Exact compiled TaskFinal2 probe (ASI/PDB hashes in build-manifest.json); sources hashed from the probe build manifest; full 3840-row log reaudited offline and preserved gzipped with the original hash. TaskSimpleFightingControl.cpp was corrected to the EXE before the run (uncommitted at the time).
functions.scope: Simple pair bench (original with hook off vs candidate with hook on), 3840 isolated CPU pairs for 7 functions of CTaskSimpleFightingControl (3) and CTaskComplexProstituteSolicit (4) with a loaded save game, zero differences, natural completion event with state_restored, layout ok, saves unchanged, configs restored. Fixtures: peds, target entity, vehicles, intelligence, player data, fake tasks (traced vtable) and a fake event (traced vtable with priority and type) in private buffers with raw EXE offsets; x87 forced to 24 bits. Compared: return value, full memory of the tested object, new pool tasks (type + words without vptr), memory of the fake tasks, fingerprint of every buffer (references masked), reference lists before and after deletion, the full trace (order and number of virtual calls and rand calls), x87 control word and empty x87 stack (FpuTag); pool m_LastFreeSlot and the 0xCD fill of free slots, patched entries, vtable slots and the time step are checked at start and restored at the end. Traced stubs, patched at the EXE address and at the DLL body and acting only on the bank thread, so these helpers get NO credit: rand 0x821B1E, FindPlayerPed 0x56E210, CPedGeometryAnalyser::ComputeEntityBoundingBoxPlanes 0x5F3660, ComputeEntityHitSide 0x5F3AC0, IsPlayerOnAMission 0x464D50, IsCoopGameGoingOn 0x441390. Run for real: FindTaskByType, GetSimplestActiveTask, GetTaskFighting, GetVehicleAppearance, IsUpsideDown, IsOnItsSide, Normalise, the task pool (tasks created by Clone are found in the pool and deleted) and references. Limits: the ProstituteSolicit destructor runs with FindPlayerPed returning null when the pool tasks created by Clone are deleted (early exit), so that deletion only proves the pool ends clean; CTaskComplexProstituteSolicit::Clone with a null client is NOT tested (the EXE and DLL constructors dereference the client). GetTaskPool/IsFreeSlotAtIndex/GetAt and the 0x80 per-slot offsets are copied from TasksBatch4. Source corrected to what the EXE does before this run: CTaskSimpleFightingControl::CalcMoveCommand (7 differences: bearing subtracted from the rotation before wrapping with a single-turn wrap; strict threshold 0x8D2E60 (0.2617993950843811) instead of DegreesToRadians(15); the EXE rand is always consumed; the 0.8 threshold compares the magnitude; vehicle sum z^2+x^2+y^2 with strict >0.7; 64-bit _ftol2 for the time step; fpatan) and its vehicle branch now calls ComputeEntityBoundingBoxPlanes (0x5F3660) instead of the UncachedAll variant; CTaskSimpleFightingControl::MakeAbortable (priorities other than 0/1/2 fall to the end instead of NOTSA_UNREACHABLE, GetEventType repeated per comparison, dot product (y*ny+z*nz)+x*nx and threshold 0.707). CTaskComplexProstituteSolicit: no source changes. Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Function-specific: Corpus 1024 (EXE 0x624B50): return values -1,0,3,7,8,9,10 observed, angle boundaries (+y axis, exact subtraction), wraps, rand with controlled low bits, extreme time steps (5e8: 32-bit overflow, negative, 0) and vehicles with fixed planes (sum-order sensitive mode); source changes listed above.

functions.scope: Simple pair bench inside the full game with a loaded save (original with the class hooks off vs candidate with the hooks on), 12736 isolated CPU pairs for 21 functions of CTaskComplexKillCriminal (8), CTaskComplexKillPedOnFootArmed (8) and CTaskSimplePlayerOnFoot (5 of 10), zero differences, natural completion event with state_restored, layout check ok, saves unchanged, configs restored. Each case rebuilds the same deterministic fixture in both legs (peds incl. a full CCopPed, criminal, partner, extras, group leader, vehicles, intelligence, player data, fake group with the leader at +0x28, fake tasks with a traced vtable (GetSubTask, GetTaskType, MakeAbortable, destructor) and quiet ones, a fake event with a traced vtable, raw EXE offsets) and compares: return value, the whole memory of the tested object (and of the second object, the partner KillCriminal task), new tasks created in the task pool (type + words without vptr), fake task memory, a fingerprint of all buffers (references masked), reference lists before and after deletion, the full trace (order and count of virtual calls, rand and collaborators), the x87 control word (24-bit precision, sqrt at 24 bits) and an empty x87 stack. Traced stubs, which get NO credit: rand (0x821B1E) and CGeneral::GetRandomNumber, CPed::SetCurrentWeapon(type), SetPedDefaultDecisionMaker, CCarCtrl::JoinCarWithRoadSystem, CPed::Say, CPedGroups::GetPedsGroup, CWorld::GetIsLineOfSightClear, CPed::GetTransformedBonePosition, CCover::FindAndReserveCoverPoint and FindCoordinatesCoverPoint, CPed::ReleaseCoverPoint, CPedIntelligence::SetTaskDuckSecondary, CTaskSimpleDuck::SetDuckTimer and ControlDuckMove, CTaskSimpleUseGun::ControlGunMove, CTaskComplexKillPedOnFootArmed::CreateSubTask (validated separately; returns a marked fake task), CCamera::Using1stPersonWeaponMode and ClearPlayerWeaponMode, CWeaponEffects::ClearCrossHair and CAnimManager::BlendAnimation; for CTaskSimplePlayerOnFoot::ProcessPed the five out-of-bench functions it calls are simulated with traces (which one is called and with what arguments). Run for real, not credited: IsPlayer, RegisterReference/CleanUpOldReference, CCopPed::AddCriminalToKill/SetPartner, CPedIntelligence::FindTaskByType/GetTaskDuck/GetTaskUseGun, CTaskManager::GetTaskSecondary, CPedGroupMembership::GetLeader, CWeapon::IsTypeMelee, CWeaponInfo, CVector::Normalise, CTimer, the task pool and the constructors/destructors of the subtasks created by KillCriminal (EnterCar, CarDrive, LeaveCar, GangDriveBy, KillPedOnFoot) on a full-size fake vehicle. CGame::currArea (0xB72914) and CLoadMonitor::m_eProcLevel (0xB7298C) are changed during LineOfSightClearForAttack and restored. Limits: of CTaskSimplePlayerOnFoot only 5 of its 10 functions are in the bench; OUT of the bench and with NO credit: PlayerControlDucked 0x687F30, PlayerControlZelda 0x6883D0, PlayerControlZeldaWeapon 0x687C20, ProcessPlayerWeapon 0x6859A0 and PlayIdleAnimations 0x6872C0 (they run the real player pad, camera, animation manager/IK, weapon system and crime reporting; ProcessPed only simulates them with traces). The vptr (word 0) and the return value are masked in the constructors and destructors (the task type through GetTaskType is compared instead of the vptr; the destructor return value, EAX, is undefined in the EXE; the final vptr of the destructor is the EXE base vtable vs the DLL one): this applies to the constructors/destructors of the bench, in particular those of CTaskComplexKillCriminal. Only the own part of each function is validated. Source corrected to what the EXE does before the approved run (uncommitted at the time; see reversing/TaskWave2A/README.md for addresses): see source_corrections_before_run. functions.scope: Simple pair bench inside the full game with a loaded save (original with the class hooks off vs candidate with the hooks on), 12864 isolated CPU pairs for 51 functions of CTrain (19), CPlane (14) and CBike (18), zero differences, natural completion event with state_restored, layout check ok, saves unchanged, configs restored. Each case rebuilds the same deterministic fixture in both legs (fake 0xA18-byte vehicles in a fake 8-slot vehicle pool that replaces the real pool pointer 0xB74494 and is restored, fake vtable with traced slots, 32-byte guards) and compares: the full hash of every vehicle, the guard, the return value, the x87 control word and the trace of outgoing calls with arguments. Virtual functions are called through the EXE vtable slot (with the hook on it points to the DLL). Traced stubs, which get NO credit: CWorld::Add/Remove, FindPlayerVehicle, CWorld::ProcessVerticalLine, CTrain::FindPositionOnTrackFromCoors, operator delete/delete[] (Shutdown only), CWorld::ClearScanCodes, TrainHitStuff, CVehicle::Render, CAutomobile::OpenDoor, CVehicle::SetModelIndex, CClumpModelInfo::FillFrameArray, CBike::ProcessRiderAnims, GetFirstObject, CAutomobile::CAutomobile, CVehicleModelInfo::GetWheelPosn, CEntity::GetColModel, CPlaceable::SetOrientation, RwFrameGetLTM, CPhysical::ApplyMoveSpeed/ApplyTurnSpeed/SkipPhysics/CheckCollision/ApplyMoveForce/ApplyTurnForce, cBuoyancy::ProcessBuoyancy, CBike::CalculateLeanMatrix and DoHeadLightBeam (Render only) and the RenderState pointers of RwGlobals. Limits: OUT of the bench and with NO credit: CTrain::ProcessControl (full train physics), CBike::Constructor, CBike::Destructor, CBike::DamageKnockOffRider (corrected in source but not benched: needs fake peds, events and CEventGroup::Add) and CBike::ProcessEntityCollision. CBike::ProcessBuoyancy is compared only without driver and passengers (m_pDriver = null, m_nMaxPassengers = 0); CBike::GetComponentWorldPosition only with present nodes (the missing-node path differs in logging); CPlane::OpenDoor with the dead-code global flag 0xC1CAFC off. Masked bench noise: in CBike::CalculateLeanMatrix the padding of the lean matrix (+0xC/+0x1C/+0x2C/+0x3C), which is stack garbage in the EXE (0x59BE30 temp + rep movs); CMatrix comparisons ignore the padding between vectors. Fixture floats are finite or quiet NaN. Only the own part of each function is validated. Source corrected to what the EXE does before the approved run (uncommitted at the time; see reversing/VehWave2/README.md for addresses): see source_corrections_before_run. Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Function-specific: Corpus 64; compared against the EXE as is.

functions.source_provenance: Exact compiled PickWeap1 probe (ASI/PDB hashes in build-manifest.json); class sources hashed from the probe build manifest and equal to the working tree at registration; full 11020-row log reaudited offline in streaming and preserved gzipped with the original hash.
functions.scope: Simple pair bench inside the full game with a loaded save (original with the function hook off vs candidate with the hook on), 11020 isolated CPU pairs for 60 pending functions of CPickups, CWeapon, ALL pairs equal, pair counts equal to the bank table, passed=true globally, natural "complete" event with state_restored, saves unchanged, configs restored. Each case rebuilds the same deterministic fixture (seed = case index) in both legs and compares the return value, the bytes of the fake objects, the touched global ranges, the x87 control word (24 bits) and the whole trace of doubled collaborators with raw arguments; foreign threads ignored. Traced doubles get NO credit. Only the own part of each function is validated. Source tested == current working tree at registration (class sources match the probe build manifest). Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. functions.scope: Banco par a par en juego completo con partida cargada; misma entrada EXE con hook RH apagado/activo. Rutas y restauración verificadas. Evidencia limitada a los fixtures del banco, no integración universal ni independencia transitiva del EXE. Alcance por función en README del banco. Validado en el worktree D:/Original/we-4 (HEAD 0ac292a76 + fuentes del lote 62). Colaboradores sustituidos por falsos identicos en ambos lados (parche de entrada en el EXE y en el cuerpo de la DLL; no se validan sus cuerpos reales): AddToQuadsAndTrianglesList (0x6E5750, sin reconstruir) en FillQuadsAndTrianglesList; CWaterLevel::GetWaterLevelNoWaves (0x6E8580) y GetGroundLevel (0x6EA8A0, sin reconstruir) en GetWaterDepth; CCamera::IsSphereVisible (0x420C40), SetUpWaterFog (0x6EA9F0), RenderHighDetailWaterRectangle_OneLayer (0x6E91D0, sin reconstruir), SplitWaterRectangleAlongXLine (0x6E73A0) y RenderWaterRectangle (0x6EC5D0) en RenderHighDetailWaterRectangle; IsSphereVisible, RenderHighDetailWaterTriangle_OneLayer (0x6E8780, sin reconstruir) y SplitWaterTriangleAlongXLine (0x6ECF00) en RenderHighDetailWaterTriangle. Las funciones de render NO se prueban contra una GPU: se comparan las llamadas a los colaboradores (que son los que escriben vertices y llaman a RenderWare) con sus argumentos exactos, en orden. El lerp (0x6E5280) NO se sustituye: la DLL usa el de WaterLevel.h y el EXE el suyo, y sus resultados se comparan en los argumentos de RenderWaterRectangle; los CRenPar de lerp se generan sin denormales (el SSE del juego vacia los denormales, el x87 no). TestLineAgainstWater y FillQuadsAndTrianglesList se prueban con un atlas de agua sintetico escrito en las tablas reales del juego (guardadas y restauradas en cada caso). Los indices de vertice 0xFFFF leen una ventana de 20 bytes anterior a m_aVertices (guardada y restaurada). GetWaterDepth: cuando GetGroundLevel devuelve true sin escribir, el EXE leeria basura de pila (no se prueba). EAX/ECX/EDX solo registrados; el AL de salida si se compara.

functions.source_provenance: Fuente propia contrastada con EXE canónico y banco RH OFF/ON dentro del juego.
functions.scope: Banco par a par en juego completo con partida cargada; misma entrada EXE con hook RH apagado/activo. Rutas y restauración verificadas. Evidencia limitada a los fixtures del banco, no integración universal ni independencia transitiva del EXE. Alcance por función en README del banco. Validado en el worktree D:/Original/we-5 (HEAD 0ac292a76 + fuente del lote 62). NO se inicializa ni se destruye el dispositivo D3D real: durante cada llamada _RwD3DDevice (0xC97C28) apunta a un dispositivo falso y todos los recursos (texturas e index buffers) son objetos COM falsos con tablas de metodos propias (Release, GetLevelCount, GetLevelDesc, GetDesc, CreateTexture, CreateIndexBuffer); el estado real de las caches (0xC87C60..0xC87FE8 y el byte 0x8D6084) se guarda antes de cada lado, se sustituye por el del caso y se restaura justo despues. Colaboradores del EXE sin reconstruir sustituidos por falsos identicos en ambos lados (no se validan sus cuerpos reales): D3DTextureBuffer::Pop (0x72FF60), Setup (0x72FE80), Push (0x72FFF0), PushWithoutIncreasingCounter (0x730AD0), Resize (0x730020), D3DIndexDataBuffer::Pop (0x730270), Resize (0x730330) y el new/delete del EXE (0x82119A / 0x8214BD, solo en el hilo del banco y con la ventana armada; fuera de ella reenvian al codigo real). Los falsos de Resize solo cambian la capacidad segun el modo del caso; los de Pop devuelven el recurso del caso sin sacarlo de la pila. Init, Shutdown y CancelBuffering se ejercitan con pilas/recursos falsos (nunca con los reales del juego). EAX/ECX/EDX solo registrados, salvo EAX (HRESULT) de CreateTexture y CreateIndexBuffer, que los llamadores del EXE (0x4CB935, 0x4CD9FE, 0x4C997C) si leen. No se prueba CreateIndexBuffer con numIndices >= 0x80000001 (grupo negativo: el EXE indexa fuera del arreglo).

Todos los colaboradores se sustituyen por falsos identicos en ambos lados (no se validan sus cuerpos ni la integracion con el mundo real): CGeneral::GetATanOfXY (0x53CC70), CWorld::FindPlayerVehicle (0x56E0D0), FindPlayerPed (0x56E210), FindPlayerCoors (0x56E010), FindPlayerSpeed (0x56E090), FindPlayerEntity (0x56E120) y ProcessLineOfSight (0x56BA00), CVector::Normalise (0x59C910), la rand() del CRT del EXE (0x821B1E), CVehicle::GetVehicleAppearance (0x6D1080), CPlaceable::AllocateMatrix (0x54F560), CSimpleTransform::UpdateMatrix (0x54F1B0), CTaskManager::GetActiveTask (0x681720) y CTask::GetTaskType (virtual), CPlane::SetGearUp (0x6CAC20), CCarCtrl::PossiblyFireHSMissile (0x429600), CCollision::DistToMathematicalLine (0x412970), CProjectileInfo::AddProjectile (0x737C80), la funcion 0x422F80 del EXE (sondeo de rumbo del avion, sin reconstruir), 0x73DF00 (lancha modelo 430, sin reconstruir) y, cuando una funcion del lote llama a otra (p. ej. GetAIHeliToAttackPlayer -> FlyAIHeliInCertainDirection / TestWhetherToFirePlaneGuns / FireHeliRocketsAtTarget), la otra tambien es un falso en esa prueba. Los vehiculos, matrices, tareas, jugador y CColPoint son imagenes falsas del banco; ningun objeto real del juego se toca. NO hay oraculo independiente en Python: la referencia es el EXE, con 4096 casos deterministas por funcion que cubren umbrales exactos (+-1 ulp), cero con signo, NaN silenciosos, infinitos, subnormales y valores enormes; los NaN son siempre silenciosos (la x87 resuelve distinto un SNaN en memoria que un QNaN en ST(0) y ningun calculo del juego produce un SNaN). Los angulos que entran en bucles de normalizacion (+-2pi) se acotan a valores finitos y moderados porque con valores enormes el original no termina. El EXE lee m_matrix de los vehiculos sin comprobar nulo en varias funciones: esos casos usan siempre matriz. Las funciones con aritmetica x87 usan ayudantes de X87Math.cpp (prefijo CcAir) compilados con /O2 /Oi /arch:IA32 /fp:fast; fsqrt/fpatan/fsin/fcos van en ayudantes separados fuera de las regiones precise (dentro saldrian como llamadas a la CRT). EAX/ECX/EDX de salida solo se registran: ningun llamador del EXE los lee (llamadores: el despachador 0x436A90 y las propias funciones del lote, comprobados con callers.py sobre todo el .text). Fuentes probadas compiladas desde el worktree D:/Original/wr-3 (HEAD 633dceef0 + source.patch del lote 65C; ver artifacts/build-manifest.json). Colaboradores sustituidos por falsos identicos en la direccion del EXE y en el cuerpo de la DLL: FxManager_c::CreateFxSystem(name,CVector) 0x4A9BE0, FxSystem_c::PlayAndKill 0x4AA3D0, FxManager_c::FxRwMatrixCreate/Destroy 0x4A9440/0x4A9460, Fx_c::CreateMatFromVec 0x49E950, FxSystem_c::CopyParentMatrix 0x4AA890, FxSystem_c::AddParticle(v3d) 0x4AA440, CObject::CObject() 0x5A1D10, CObject::SetIsStatic 0x5A0760, CEntity::SetModelIndex 0x532AE0, CVehicle::ClearGettingOutFlags 0x6D3060, CVehicleAnimGroup::GetGroup 0x6E3B00 y la ranura 28 de la vtable del vehiculo (ProcessOpenDoor, falso en una vtable de arena); el banco compara la traza completa de esas llamadas, el objeto/matriz/tarea resultante y el resto de la arena. Ningun llamador del EXE lee EAX/ECX/EDX de las funciones Fx ni del callback (solo registrados); los tres llamadores de CProjectile::CProjectile leen EAX = this (exigido aparte). El vptr del constructor es el de la vtable de la DLL (como CObject/CPed). El callback es cdecl (el llamador retira los 8 bytes de argumentos). Fx.cpp se compila con las opciones SSE por defecto del proyecto: la distancia a la camara y el filtro `> 625.0` coinciden con el x87 del EXE salvo en el exponente extendido, que solo afecta a magnitudes que ya superan 625.

La funcion no llama a ninguna otra: no hay colaboradores sustituidos. La aritmetica x87 de 24 bits vive en X87Math.cpp (Wl67SeaBedSegmentCpp). El banco guarda, rellena por caso y restaura la region del bufer temporal de agua [0xC4B950, 0xC5F958) (contadores, indices y vertices) y vigila 0x40 bytes a cada lado. Los contadores previos se prueban en 0..2044 (vertices) y 0..4090 (indices): la funcion no comprueba el desbordamiento del bufer y el banco no lo provoca. Los dos llamadores del EXE (0x6EF822, 0x6EF861) no leen EAX/ECX/EDX.

GetInstance (0x4684F0) sigue llamando al constructor por su direccion del EXE (que ahora salta al hook); su banco no forma parte de este.
